title: Spending and Summary Tabs
subtitle: Spending becomes the page for this month, with averages beside it and rent counted from the 1st. Account balances move to the top of Financial Summary. The Dashboard tab is retired. One upgrade, one tick, one sync.
intro: After the pull request merges, the code is already in your Sheet. The upgrade redraws the Spending and Financial Summary tabs and puts the old Dashboard tab away.

**What does not change:** no rows, balances or entered values. Transactions, Income, Debts and every other data tab stay exactly as they are. The month you had selected and your checklist ticks carry over to the Spending tab.
This upgrade also covers the two earlier changes from today (paychecks counted from the deposit, and the pay stub reminder) if you have not run it since.

steps.text: In the Sheet, open **File → Version history → Name current version** and name it `Before two-tab layout 2026-11-12`.
Open the **App Setup** tab and check that **Build Script Version** reads `1.14.0`. If it shows an older number, the new code has not arrived yet; wait a minute and reload the Sheet.
steps.note: This is the check that stops an upgrade from running on the old code.

steps.text: Open **Finance Tracker → Upgrade workbook (keeps data)** and confirm.
steps.done: The report includes a line that starts with "Dashboard tab retired". When it finishes you are on the Spending tab, and the Dashboard tab is no longer in the tab strip.

steps.text: Open **Recurring Payments** and find the **Rent** row. Scroll right to the new last column, **Record Automatically?**, and tick the box on that row.
steps.note: This tells the tracker to count rent from the 1st of every month at the amount on that row, without waiting for the bank. Only tick it for a bill that is the same every month. If the new row has not appeared after a minute, carry on: the sync in the next step adds it.
steps.done: Within a few seconds a new row appears at the bottom of **Transactions**: "Rent (recorded automatically)", dated the 1st of this month, for the rent amount.

steps.text: Open **Finance Tracker → Bank feed → Sync now**.
steps.note: The Venmo payment from November 2 that you had marked Housing is waiting on Import Staging. I gave it the subcategory Mortgage or Rent, so this sync brings it in as a rent payment.
steps.done: On Transactions, the Venmo payment is there as Housing / Mortgage or Rent, and the "Rent (recorded automatically)" row has gone down by exactly that payment. Together they add up to one month of rent.

steps.text: From now on, when a Venmo payment for rent shows on **Import Staging**, give it **Category** Housing and **Subcategory** Mortgage or Rent, and tick Reviewed? as usual.
steps.note: Each rent payment you categorize takes that much off the automatic entry. When the payments add up to the full rent, the automatic entry is marked deleted. Rent is never counted twice, and you do not have to do anything else.
steps.done: On the Spending tab, Housing includes the full rent, and the Recurring bills hover list shows Rent with how much has been paid so far.

steps.text: At the top, **Month** (cell B3) shows the month you had selected on the Dashboard. To look at another month, type any date in that month here.
steps.done: Below it you see the review banner, then Expected Take-Home and Spent So Far, then Current Flexible Spending with this week's three boxes.

steps.text: Look at **Compare with** (cell E3). It is a dropdown: last 3, 6 or 12 full months, or the same 3 months last year. It decides which months make up the "typical month" everywhere on the tab, and the small line beside it names the months counted.
steps.note: Your transactions start in November, so for now Typical Month shows a dash and the line says no full month is recorded yet. The averages fill in on December 1. "Same 3 months last year" needs a year of history.

steps.text: Rest the mouse on the **Fixed vs flexible** tile (the label, the number or the small line under it). A note opens listing what counted as fixed and what counted as flexible this month, largest first, with who was paid. Do the same on **Needs vs wants** and on **Recurring bills**, which lists every recurring bill with its amount, when it is due and whether this month's payment has been seen.
steps.note: A small dark triangle in the corner of a cell means it has a note. The lists refresh on their own with every sync and when you change the month, a transaction or a recurring bill; each one says when it was last written.
steps.done: The recurring list includes the nanny as a weekly bill, with its monthly amount beside it. If anything sits under the wrong heading, change its Spending Type or Need/Want on Transactions and the list follows.

steps.text: Scroll to **By category**. The columns are This Month, Budget, Last Month, Typical Month and Used, then the bar. Once there is a typical month, each bar fills toward it and turns red if the category goes past it.
steps.done: The categories and amounts for this month match what you saw before. No cell shows an error such as #NAME?, #REF! or #ERROR!. If one does, tell me which cell.

steps.text: Scroll further down to **Average spending by category**. This is the sideways bar graph: one bar per category, largest first.
steps.note: It is empty until December for the same reason. The note under it says so.

steps.text: At the bottom, the **Monthly Review Checklist** has the same ticks it had on the Dashboard.
Open **Financial Summary**. The top now shows checking, savings (with the faded "Savings + bill transfers" line under it) and the three cards with what is owed and when each is due.
steps.done: The balances match what the Dashboard showed. Everything that was on this tab before is still there, a little lower on the page.
The lines about the Spending tab cards, the Typical Month and the Financial Summary accounts block all pass.

steps.text: Nothing to do. The Dashboard tab is emptied and hidden, not deleted, so nothing breaks if a bookmark still points to it.
steps.note: If you want it gone for good: open **View → Hidden sheets** and pick Dashboard to bring it back, then right-click its tab and choose Delete. Everything it showed now lives on Spending and Financial Summary.
